transcript:
Meeting header
Date/Time: 2026-12-10 15:00 PST
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Dana Morales (Nova - Head of ML), Mark Liu (Nova - Platform Eng), Sara Bennett (Nova - CTO)

Summary: Quick POC scoping focused on cost/unit economics and workload sizing. Discussed three primary workloads (chat assistant, document summarization, embeddings for search), rough qps/token estimates, batching/caching knobs, quantization options, and budget constraints. Agreed next steps: share pricing sheet, Nova to provide sample traces, Redwood to run a 48-hour benchmark, schedule security/VPC follow-up.

Topics: success criteria; p95 latency targets; request and token volumes; per-token cost estimates; batching window and batch size; prefix/KV cache benefits; dedicated vs hosted cost tradeoffs; quantization and model sizing; pilot timeline and acceptance criteria.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Jamie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jamie from Redwood, AE on the account, with Samir our solutions engineer. How's it going?
[00:10] Dana: Good, thanks. Dana here. We've been evaluating a few inference vendors and want to scope a POC focused on cost realism \u000E2\u00128\u001A particularly per-token economics for our customer support assistant and document pipeline.
[00:20] Jamie: Great, that's exactly what we wanted to walk through \u000E2\u00128\u001A success criteria, workload sizing, and what real unit costs look like once you factor batching and caching.
[00:30] Samir: Quick intro from me. I'll talk latency/throughput tradeoffs, recommended batch windows, and how our KV/prefix caching reduces effective tokens.
[00:40] Sara: From Nova's side, primary constraints: p95 for chat must be <750ms, budget for pilot is $10k/month, and we'd like the POC to mimic production traffic for two weeks.
[01:05] Mark: For volumes, we expect peak 50 qps for chat, average 15 qps sustained. Average tokens per generation around 180, sometimes up to 600 for long summaries. Embeddings workload is batched offline, roughly 500k vectors/day.
[01:35] Samir: Ok that gives a useful baseline. Quick back-of-envelope: 15 qps * 180 tokens * 3600 * 24 => ~233M tokens/day, wait no that sounds high, let me re-check math.
[01:50] Dana: Sorry, our numbers are: 15 sustained concurrent requests, not per-second. So more like 15 reqs/s during business hours peak, average 5 reqs/s global.
[02:10] Samir: Thanks, that clarifies. Using 5 rps avg and 180 tokens/request => 900 tokens/sec => ~77.8M tokens/day. For a two-week POC that's ~1.1B tokens.
[02:30] Jamie: Important to separate hosted per-token cost vs dedicated commit. For hosted we estimate per-token model cost varies by model and quantization. For example, unoptimized 70B fp16 might be roughly $0.0009/token end-to-end in our hosted pricing sheet; quantized int8 variants can reduce compute to ~0.0003-0.0005/token depending on batch efficiency.
[02:55] Mark: Those are big deltas. Can you explain where the savings come from?
[03:05] Samir: Sure \u000E2\u00128\u00136 three levers: batching efficiency (amortize kernel setup across multiple requests), KV/prefix cache (avoid re-sending prompt tokens on follow-ups, which for chat can shave 20\u000E2\u000080\t340% of tokens), and quantization (reduces memory footprint and allows higher throughput per GPU). Also routing to smaller model variants for lower-cost routes.
[03:30] Dana: Realistically, we can't tolerate latency degradation. How does batching affect p95?
[03:40] Samir: We typically use short batch windows \u000E2\u000080\t350ms for chat to preserve latency. For your throughput, a 25ms window with adaptive batching will give good GPU utilization without blowing up p95; we still aim to keep p95 under 750ms. For long summaries batching can be larger (100\u000E2\u000080\t200ms) since you're more throughput-sensitive there.
[04:05] Sara: What about KV caching numbers \u000E2\u00128\u00139 can you quantify savings?
[04:10] Samir: In prior customers with sessioned assistants we see effective token reduction of 25\u000E2\u000080\t35% because the system reuses cached KV states for prefixes and common instructions. For workflows where users repeatedly ask follow-ups, the savings are higher.
[04:25] Jamie: On the financials \u000E2\u00128\u00141 assuming Nova's POC token volume of ~1.1B tokens over two weeks, rough hosted estimates: if using a quantized 70B variant at $0.00045/token that's ~$495k \u000E2\u00128\u00141 which obviously is out of budget; but with caching and batching the effective billed tokens might drop to ~700M and with dedicated reserved capacity pricing we can get unit costs down by ~3x compared to hosted.
[04:55] Dana: That hosted number is way above our $10k/mo pilot. So the POC must use model selection and optimization to stay within budget. What are realistic cheap model combos?
[05:05] Samir: For cost-constrained pilots we recommend a multi-tier approach: 1) Use a smaller base model for short queries (e.g., 13B quantized) for the majority of traffic; 2) Route long summaries and high-quality responses to larger quantized variants; 3) Use embeddings offline and cache results for search to avoid recomputing. For 13B int8, hosted effective cost can be ~0.00006\u000E2\u000080\t0.00012/token depending on batching.
[05:40] Mark: If we route 80% of requests to 13B and 20% to quantized 70B, what's back-of-envelope cost?
[05:50] Samir: Quick calc: with 1.1B tokens total, assume after caching effective tokens 700M. 80% on 13B at $0.00009/token => 448M * 0.00009 ~ $40k. 20% on 70B at $0.00045 => 140M * 0.00045 ~ $63k. Total ~$103k for two weeks \u000E2\u00128\u00141 still above. But switching to dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit) we can cut the 70B line to ~$0.00015/token and 13B to ~$0.00003/token \u000E2\u00128\u00141 then total is ~448M*0.00003 = $13.4k + 140M*0.00015 = $21k => $34.4k for two weeks; still over $10k but closer.
[06:40] Dana: Dedicated sounds promising but commit is a hard sell internally. Could we scope a smaller POC: fewer users, trimmed token limits, and heavier caching to fit $10k?
[06:55] Jamie: Absolutely \u000E2\u00128\u00141 we usually run a staged POC. Option A: functional smoke test using 100k tokens/day for two weeks to validate latency and integration. Option B: production-like throughput but reduced window \u000E2\u00128\u00149 say 25% of real traffic \u000E2\u00128\u00149 to stress routing and metrics. We can produce cost estimates for both.
[07:20] Mark: For benchmarking, what do you need from us?
[07:25] Samir: Sample traces (prompts + token counts), 24\u000E2\u000080\u001348 hours of representative traffic, and a set of success criteria: p50/p95 latency targets, accuracy thresholds on a small eval set, and budget ceiling. We'll instrument the run with per-token cost breakdowns.
[07:45] Dana: Success criteria: p95 < 750ms for chat; average accuracy drop < 3% vs our baseline; total POC spend < $10k. If we can't hit cost target we may extend to a reserved discussion with finance.
[08:05] Sara: On security, we need SOC2 attestations, audit logs, SSO (SAML), and KMS integration for keys. Also VPC peering is required for the private deployment test.
[08:20] Jamie: Noted \u000E2\u00128\u00141 we have SOC2 and ISO docs, SAML support, and KMS integrations. For private deployments we can do a VPC/Tunnel setup or on-prem package. We'll add a security follow-up with our infra team.
[08:35] Mark: Any benchmarks you can share that show cost per token vs batch size?
[08:40] Samir: Yes \u000E2\u00128\u00141 in our internal runs increasing batch size from 1 to ~8 at 25ms window typically gives 2.5\u000E2\u000080\t3x throughput boost depending on model. For example, a single A100-class GPU with a quantized 13B can handle ~150\u000E2\u000080\t250 tokens/sec at batch sizes 4\u000E2\u000080\t8; 70B quantized does ~600\u000E2\u000080\t900 tokens/sec with larger memory-optimized GPUs. We will include these numbers in the spreadsheet.
[09:15] Dana: How do you handle fallbacks if a large model is unavailable?
[09:20] Jamie: Smart routing \u000E2\u00128\u00141 we can fallback to smaller model variants automatically, or route to dedicated pools first and then hosted burst. Policies are configurable so SLAs are preserved.
[09:35] Mark: For caching, do you bill all tokens or only new tokens?
[09:40] Samir: Billing is on generated tokens and consumed model compute; with KV cache we don't re-send prompt tokens to the model so effective billed tokens are lower. We'll show examples with and without prefix caching in the cost sheet.
[09:55] Dana: Timelines \u000E2\u00128\u00141 how long to stand up the POC and run benchmarks?
[10:00] Jamie: If Nova can provide traces by Monday (2026-12-13), we can spin up a POC harness and run a 48-hour benchmark by 2026-12-17, with initial results same week and a short follow-up on security the following week.
[10:20] Samir: For the benchmark we'll run three configurations: hosted small-model heavy, hosted mixed, and a dedicated small-commit sim. We'll report p50/p95, tokens per second, effective billed tokens after cache, and per-token cost.
[10:45] Mark: For the dedicated scenario what kind of commit is typical to hit the quoted 3x savings?
[10:50] Jamie: Typically a 3\u000E2\u000080\u0000936 month reserved commit for GPU capacity gives the best unit economics. Minimums vary by region and model size; we can get specific once we know the target sustained RPS. For a short pilot we can sometimes do a 1-month commit or pilot discount to demonstrate the economics.
[11:10] Dana: Any gotchas on embeddings cost? We batch offline but if we need to refresh vectors daily how expensive is that?
[11:20] Samir: Embeddings are more predictable; you pay per embedding call and it's usually much cheaper per token equivalent because models are smaller and run in large batches. For 500k vectors/day we can estimate an operational cost and show tradeoffs between incremental updates vs full rebuild.
[11:40] Sara: One more question: Do you expose per-route cost breakdowns in the console? We need visibility for ops.
[11:45] Jamie: Yes \u000E2\u00128\u00141 Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdown per route/model, plus tracing and error analysis so you can map feature to cost. We'll include screenshots and sample dashboards.
[12:05] Mark: Ok let's recap next steps.
[12:10] Jamie: Recap \u000E2\u00128\u00141 Jamie will send pricing + spreadsheet; Samir will prepare benchmark harness and test configs; Nova to provide traces and define final success criteria; schedule security/VPC follow-up.
[12:25] Dana: That works. Appreciate the clear options \u000E2\u00128\u00141 staging the POC to fit the $10k budget while proving performance makes sense.
[12:35] Jamie: Great \u000E2\u00128\u00141 we'll follow up by email with attachments. Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
